validated_work_order.understanding: The weekly end-bound suite exists twice and runs twice on every test run. packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/weekly-end-date.test.ts is 338 lines with 10 `it(...)`; custom-spreadsheet.test.ts is 1100 lines and carries all ten of those titles under `weekly custom report end bound` (line 380, seven cases) and `weekly grouped report end bound` (line 504, three cases). I re-verified the comparison the epic asked for rather than carrying v1's finding over. The ten `it('...')` titles extracted from each file are identical. Diffing the two describe blocks returns 76 changed lines across 11 hunks, and filtering those 76 lines for `expect|toEqual|toBe|toHave` returns nothing: no assertion, expected value or snapshot line differs anywhere. Every hunk is the props wrapper alone, `runCustom({...})` against `runCustom(weeklyProps({...}))`. The weeklyRows fixture is byte-identical (md5 6342ab83b4f60f70b3f77d129ec0d601). The category fixtures are the same two objects under different const names (categories/categoryGroups at lines 27-35 of the shorter file, weeklyCategories/weeklyCategoryGroups at 320-328 of the survivor). weeklyProps supplies precisely the defaults the shorter file's own runCustom already defaulted to, plus `balanceTypeOp: undefined`, which sortData.ts:24 already guards with `if (!balanceTypeOp || !sortByOp) return () => 0`. So the comparison resolves one way: weekly-end-date.test.ts contributes no unique case and is deleted outright, nothing folded back. A repo-wide grep for 'weekly-end-date' returns no hit outside the file's own path, and vitest discovers tests by the glob at vite.config.mts:406, so nothing has to be unlisted along with the deletion.
validated_work_order.root_cause: The suite was copied rather than moved into custom-spreadsheet.test.ts during a merge-conflict resolution. b593293 ('[AI] Fix weekly reports truncating the final week to one day (#12)', already an ancestor of main) added the ten cases to custom-spreadsheet.test.ts; the merge commit 9c44b8d cited in the issue is not reachable in this checkout, but the copy is demonstrably present on main. The last commit touching either file is 026f8b6, the #9 category-filtering fix, so both copies are still maintained by later work and neither has rotted out of use.
validated_work_order.approach:
Delete weekly-end-date.test.ts outright and change nothing else. No case needs to move: the ten titles and their bodies already exist in custom-spreadsheet.test.ts, verified by diff rather than by eye, so the epic's 'fold back whatever it uniquely adds' reduces to a plain delete. custom-spreadsheet.test.ts is not edited except for one comment block recording the comparison — editing it further would widen a diff whose whole point is that it is a deletion.

This plan addresses the one objection raised against v1: v1 required the release note to state the comparison and what it found (AC-2.how_to_verify, AC-3.how_to_verify, qa_script step 6) while files[2] specified a release note whose body said only that the tests ran twice and now run once, so an implementer following files[] exactly would have produced a note that failed its own acceptance criteria. The direction chosen narrows that obligation to one artefact: the full comparison — what was compared, what the diff showed, and the conclusion that there was no unique case — is required in the code comment block above `describe('weekly custom report end bound', ...)` and nowhere else. The release note is required only to exist, carry `category: Maintenance` and an `authors:` list, and say the duplicate weekly end-date suite was removed, which is what the repo's own release-note convention asks for ('keep it short and clear — ideally one sentence'; clarify-sqljs-fetch-patch-test-comment.md is a Maintenance note whose whole body is one clause). AC-2, AC-3 and qa_script step 6 have been rewritten to match files[] exactly, so no two artefacts in this work order disagree. Per .github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md the PR template is left blank, so the comparison cannot go in the PR Description — it goes in the code comment, which is part of the PR's diff.

After the change, run the same command: each of the ten titles appears exactly once, under `weekly custom report end bound` and `weekly grouped report end bound` in custom-spreadsheet.test.ts, and the passed count is ten lower. No test outside those ten changes result.

alternatives_considered.approach: Delete weekly-end-date.test.ts and move anything unique into custom-spreadsheet.test.ts.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: There is nothing to move. The diff over the two describe blocks contains no assertion line at all, the ten titles are identical, and the bodies differ only in the props wrapper, whose defaults are the ones the shorter file already defaulted to. This was the epic's first option and it reduces to a plain delete.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep weekly-end-date.test.ts and delete the ten cases from custom-spreadsheet.test.ts instead.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It keeps the weaker of the two suites. The survivor would lose the server double that applies `$transform` precision and splits the amount filter, and it would strand the `weeklyProps` helper, which the weekly budgeted describe also uses. It also means editing a 1100-line file to delete ten cases rather than deleting a 338-line file outright.

alternatives_considered.approach: Extract the ten cases plus their fixtures and server double into a shared test helper both files import.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It leaves both files running the same ten cases, which is the duplication the ticket exists to remove — it hides the duplication behind an import instead of ending it, and it adds a shared helper to a codebase trying to lose a file, not gain a layer.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep weekly-end-date.test.ts but mark the ten cases `it.skip`, or move them under a single shared describe imported by both.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Skipped tests still count in a reportable total, so AC-1's 'drops by exactly ten' would fail; and the shared-describe form keeps two files alive for one suite. Either leaves the 338 lines a reviewer is asked to judge, which the ticket names as half the cost.

alternatives_considered.approach: Record the comparison in both the code comment and the release note, as v1's AC-2/AC-3/qa_script step 6 required.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This is the objection v1 was rejected for. It cannot be carried out by the implementer: the repo's release-note convention says one sentence, and the existing precedent for a Maintenance note of this kind is a single clause with no narrative. Requiring both means the release note either violates the repo convention or fails the plan's own acceptance criteria. The obligation is therefore narrowed to the code comment, and AC-2, AC-3 and qa_script step 6 have been rewritten to match.

validated_work_order.debate_summary: v1 was rejected on one objection, an internal inconsistency between two parts of the same work order: AC-2.how_to_verify, AC-3.how_to_verify and qa_script step 6 all required the release note to state that a comparison was made and what it found, while files[2] specified a release note whose one-sentence body said only that the tests ran twice and now run once. An implementer following files[] exactly would therefore have produced a note that failed the plan's own acceptance criteria. The reviewer's recommended direction — narrow the obligation to the code comment — is the one taken here. The full comparison (what was compared, that the ten `it` titles were identical, that the diff showed only the props wrapper and no differing assertion, and that nothing was folded back) is now required in the code comment block above `describe('weekly custom report end bound', ...)` and nowhere else; the release note is held only to the repo's own convention (exists, `category: Maintenance`, `authors:` list, one sentence saying the duplicate suite was removed). AC-2, AC-3 and qa_script step 6 were rewritten to match files[] exactly, with explicit wording telling QA not to fail the release note for omitting the comparison narrative. The technical finding was re-verified from scratch rather than carried over: it is unchanged and now rests on a stronger check than title comparison — filtering the 76 changed lines of the describe-block diff for any assertion yields nothing.
residual_risks: The AC-1 and AC-5 test-count deltas are the only claims here not directly executed, because this checkout has no node_modules state and vitest cannot start. Both are stated as measurements to take against main, not as results.
